background-color.title: background-color Property
background-color.history: The background-color property sets the background color of an element.
background-color.tip: Use background-color when you want to give an element a solid background color. You can use color names, HEX, RGB, HSL, and other CSS color values.

background-clip.title: background-clip Property
background-clip.history: The background-clip property controls where an element's background is allowed to appear: the border, padding, or content area.
background-clip.tip: Use background-clip when you want to control how far the background color or image extends. For example, content-box keeps the background inside the content area and does not paint behind the padding or border.

background-shorthand.tip: Use background as a shorter way to set multiple background properties together, such as color, image, repeat, position, and size. It can make your CSS cleaner and easier to manage.

tables-layout.title: Tables for Layout (Legacy)
tables-layout.history: Tables were originally meant for tabular data but misused in the 90s for page layouts. They are heavy and not semantic.
tables-layout.tip: Avoid using HTML tables for page layout. Tables should be used for actual tabular data, while CSS Flexbox and Grid are better choices for creating modern page layouts.

flexbox.title: Flexbox Layout
flexbox.history: Flexbox is a modern one-dimensional layout system for arranging items in rows or columns. Perfect for navbars, cards, and forms.
flexbox.tip: Use Flexbox when you need to arrange elements in a single row or column. Combine properties such as justify-content, align-items, gap, and flex-direction to control the layout.

subgrid.title: Subgrid Feature
subgrid.history: Subgrid allows child elements to inherit parent grid tracks for consistent alignment.
subgrid.tip: Use subgrid when nested grid items need to align with the rows or columns defined by their parent grid. It helps keep complex layouts consistently aligned without recreating the same grid tracks.

multi-column-power.title: Multi-column Layout
multi-column-power.history: The multi-column layout creates newspaper-style columns for text content. Useful for magazines and articles.
multi-column-power.tip: Use multi-column layout for long blocks of text that work well when split into columns. Adjust column-count or column-width and use column-gap to control spacing between columns.

transition.title: transition
transition.history: Smoothly animate property changes (hover, focus, class toggles). Simple and performant for UI micro-interactions.
transition.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>transition Example</title>
  <style>
    body {
      font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
      padding: 24px;
      background: #080c16;
    }
    .btn {
      background: #2563eb;
      color: #fff;
      padding: 12px 18px;
      border-radius: 8px;
      transition: all 0.3s ease;
      display: inline-block;
      border: none;
      cursor: pointer;
    }
    .btn:hover {
      transform: translateY(-6px);
      background: #1e40af;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn">Hover me</button>
</body>
</html>
transition.quiz: Which property creates smooth hover/focus transitions?
